item.title: North Carolina Central narrowly beat Michael Vick, Norfolk State 29-28
item.description: North Carolina Central narrowly beat Michael Vick, Norfolk State 29-28 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . North Carolina Central secured a come-from-behind victory over Michael Vick’s Norfolk State Spartans , 29-28. Norfolk State appeared to be taking control when a Jalyn Daniels touchdown to open the fourth quarter put the Spartans up 28-17. North Carolina Central answered right away. The Eagles put together a seven-play, 75-yard drive that Jones finished with a 7-yard keeper, cutting the deficit to 28-23 with more than 11 minutes left to play. The ending turned on two late fumbles and a missed kick. Gino Addison, who ran for a game-high 174 yards on 18 carries, fumbled, and Norfolk State recovered with 1:27 remaining. Quarterback Deljay Bailey then ran for 13 yards but fumbled it right back to Central. Jones found Wall for the 26-yard touchdown that put the Eagles ahead 29-28 with 27 seconds left. Norfolk State still had a chance. After an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty on North Carolina Central, the Spartans moved into range, and Marco Peery lined up for a 37-yard field goal attempt with four seconds left that missed. Now, Michael Vick continues to look for his first win in the MEAC after losing against DeSean Jackson’s Delaware State Hornets in the Battle Of The Legends last week. They now prepare to face South Carolina State . The Eagles have yet to beat South Carolina State since Chennis Berry took over the program for a departing Buddy Pough in the 2024 season. item.title: Matt Campbell updates condition of Penn State football legend Jack Ham
item.description: SEATTLE − Legendary Penn State football player and longtime radio broadcaster Jack Ham was in stable condition in the University of Washington Medical Center Saturday evening, Nov. 7, according to university officials, after undergoing a medical emergency here before the Nittany Lions ' game. Ham, 77, was rushed to the hospital an hour or so before Penn State began their eventual 28-25 victory here in Husky Stadium. After the game, head coach Matt Campbell began his press conference by addressing Ham − and the apparent efforts to help him to safety and a hopeful recovery from his an undisclosed medical situation. Campbell singled out longtime radio partner and play-by-play announcer Steve Jones, who apparently was by Ham's side when he fell ill. The Lions (5-4, 2-4 Big Ten) held on to beat Washington with a dramatic save at the end. "Everybody knows that man, this was a gut-wrenching day for Penn State football with Jack Ham,” Campbell said. “Obviously, a really tough situation as we got off the buses here (at the stadium). “First of all, I think we should all know Steve Jones and the heroic effort that he did for somebody he loves dearly. And if it’s not for Steve, you know, and what he did, I don’t know if we would have as good a news as we do right now. And then I want to also thank the University of Washington, their athletic director, their emergency team were incredible. They were outstanding. I think, hopefully, as all of you know, Jack is in stable condition right now, and obviously, the emotion of that." Penn State went on to play their best first half of football of the season in leading the Huskies 28-6 at halftime − before holding off a second-half surge and desperately hanging on. “What I was really proud of our football team, and we talked about a little bit before we went out to the game," Campbell said. "Just the courage of our kids to play with what Jack Ham means to Penn State football, how that guy played the game, how that guy still to this day serves our football program. It was awesome to be able to go win the football game for him and his family, and our thoughts and prayers will continue to be with him on a full recovery.” Penn State officials were not disclosing the nature of Ham's medical issue or any further details yet on his condition. The Johnstown, Pa. native has worked for more than two decades with Jones, the pair calling their 300th game in 2023. Ham was a consensus All-American linebacker at Penn State and the 34th player taken in the 1971 NFL Draft. He would go on to win four Super Bowls with the Pittsburgh Steelers and would be regarded as one of the best linebackers in NFL history with a particular supremacy as a pass defender. Ham was named the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year in 1975 and made eight straight Pro Bowls. Frank Bodani covers Penn State football for the York Daily Record and USA Today Network. BVB jumped out to a 2-0 lead, but let Elversberg back in the game thanks to a Golazo from Noel Futkeu. Thankfully, the visitors could not find an equalizer, despite playing in front of a record away crowd , and Dortmund now can head into the break without any dropped points hanging over their heads. Niko Kovac deployed his troops in a 4-3-3 with Fabio Silva leading the line, Carney Chukwuemeka and Konstantinos Karetsas on the wings, and Joey Veerman, Felix Nmecha, and Jobe Bellingham in midfield. Joane Gadou got the start again, this time as a right-back. Dortmund did a great job shutting down Elversberg in the first half, with the away side only mustering four shot attempts and 0.09 xG. Dortmund’s midfield was suffocating, and the attacking trio looked deadly. Unfortunately, Chukwuemeka suffered a muscle injury and was subbed off in the 34th minute. While BVB had the better of the chances, including Fabio Silva scoring from near the half-way line and Karetsas creating multiple chances, the half ended 0-0. item.title: Penn State postgame report card: Grading Nittany Lions vs. Washington
item.description: They sweated it out in the end, but the Nittany Lions were able to pull out a victory over the Washington Huskies 28-25. Carson Hansen and Chase Sowell starred in an electrifying first half display where the Nittany Lions had 303 total yards, more than they ha in Big Ten games this season. Still, there was a worrying comeback attempt that exposed the defensive frailties that occurred pre-bye week. That's why this game wasn't perfect. Still, the Nittany Lions come away with a second straight Big Ten win and is looking like they could potentially contend for bowl eligibility. Here is a look at the postgame report card for the Nittany Lions against Washington. Quarterback: B For some reason, Rocco Becht can never have a complete Big Ten performance. In the first half of the game, Becht was 11 of 17 for 193 yards and 2 touchdowns. His chemistry with both Zay Robinson and Chase Sowell was on point and it allowed the Nittany Lions to score with ease on four of six first half possessions. Then the second half came. He only completed five passes for 47 yards and didn't lead a single scoring drive. Had the Nittany Lions blown this lead, he probably wouldn't have heard the end of it from fans. Still, he did enough to win and did not turn the ball over, albeit with a couple nervy moments sprinkled in. Running Backs: B+ This was more of an efficient rather than an explosive performance by the Penn State running backs. Unlike last week, they were held under 200 yards and it was a similar committee approach. As predicted, Carson Hansen shown early and was the leading rusher for the squad with 119 yards on 14 carries and a 12 yard touchdown. Meanwhile, Cam Wallace had the other rushing touchdown on the day and finished with 56 yards. While not the breakout game of last week, they played a pivotal role in how the blue and white won this game. Receivers and Tight Ends: B+ Where would the Nittany Lions be without the play of Chase Sowell ? Back from injury, Sowell was easily the brightest offensive star for the Nittany Lions on the day. He had four catches for 125 yards and a touchdown as well as several highlight reel catches. Other than that however, there was nothing of note from the rest of the corps, as the next best receiver was Brett Eskildsen with four catches for 36 yards. Still, it's nice to know that a player of Sowell's caliber can carry the weight for a Jekyll and Hyde offense. Defense: C+ Much like with Rocco Becht, it was a tale of two halves for the Penn State defense. After only allowing only 6 points and 114 yards for the entire first half, they gave up 183 and 19 points in the second half. Demond Williams Jr. went from only throwing for 36 yards to 172. They also continue to struggle to contain the running as six running backs for the Huskies combined for 134 yards on the ground. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Brooklyn Nets - Jordan Farmar
item.description: The Brooklyn Nets have signed, drafted, and traded for players from virtually every state in the US, and much of the wider world beyond the United States. From Alabama to Wyoming, and from Australia to Ukraine, the Nets have a long and distinguished history of turning over every stone to find the talent needed to succeed in the NBA. From their start in the American Basketball Association (ABA) as the New Jersey Americans and New York Nets to their jump to the NBA as the New Jersey Nets right through to today, the organization has cast their net for talent wide since the inception of the ball club. For this installment of our series documenting the provenience of every Nets player to suit up for the franchise, let's take a look at every player from California who has played for Brooklyn. Our focus in this article is Jordan Farmar. An alum of UCLA, he was picked up with the 26th overall selection of the 2006 NBA Draft by the Los Angeles Lakers. The Los Angeles, California native played the first 4 seasons of his pro career with Los Angeles, coming to an end when he signed with the Brooklyn Nets in 2010. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to the Atlanta Hawks in 2012. During his time suiting up for the Nets, Farmar put up 9.9 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 4.4 assists per game. item.title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 40 - Ryan Bowen (2004-06)
item.description: The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history. To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day. With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover. And for today's article, we will continue with the eighth of eight who wore the No. 40, Ryan Bowen. After ending his college career at Iowa, Bowen was picked up with the 55th overall selection of the 1998 NBA Draft by the Denver Nuggets. The Fort Madison, Iowa native played the first 5 seasons of his NBA career with Denver, coming to an end when he signed with the Houston Rockets in 2004. His stay with the team lasted until he was cut in 2006. During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Bowen wore only jersey No. 40 and put up 1.5 points and 1.2 rebounds per game. item.title: Mike Florio plans to ‘ignore’ Dianna Russini’s reporting at Pro Football Talk until ‘credibility is somehow restored’
item.description: Credit: PFT Live; The Rich Eisen Show All signs are pointing toward Dianna Russini returning to NFL media next week with a new weekly podcast. The question now is what form her content will take. Will Russini attempt to slide back into her role as an insider? Is her plan to continue to break news? And most importantly, will she address her alleged affair with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel? As the leader of one of the most important platforms in the NFL, Mike Florio is pushing publicly for these answers. Florio not only hosts PFT Live for NBC Sports and contributes to Football Night In America , but he also runs Pro Football Talk, the news site that aggregates all of the league’s latest news and rumors in one place and is widely read by fans and industry insiders. In the latest episode of PFT Live , Florio stated that he plans to “ignore” any news from Russini “unless the credibility is somehow restored.” As Florio sees it, the starting point is that Russini must address what happened with Vrabel. Florio noted that so far, Russini’s only two public comments on the matter were both denials. In the initial article that broke the story open at the New York Post , Russini denied she had any relationship with Vrabel. When she resigned from The Athletic, she accused the media of stretching the truth. “If there’s going to be actual reporting as part of this, you’ve gotta have some credibility, or nobody’s going to believe what you say,” Florio said. “Is there going to be an effort to be an insider again? Unless and until we get an explanation that restores credibility… as somebody who aggregates the reports of others, amplifies the reports of others, wants my audience to believe the reporting of others, I’ve gotta believe it first. “And after everything that’s happened, everything we know, I’m not going to be inclined to believe anything. Which means I’m not going to be amplifying anything. I don’t care what the reporting is. Unless and until it’s confirmed by someone who doesn’t have these credibility issues, I’m going to ignore it. Unless the credibility is somehow restored.” Russini appears to be partnering with BetUS on the weekly show, as well as a written column. She reportedly hired a crisis publicist to help with her return. In an internal report at The Athletic released earlier this year , the outlet’s standards editor stated that Russini’s relationship was a “violation” of standards. The editor found multiple instances of improper attribution of information related to Vrabel and his teams, as well as a video interview that called into question how Russini got access to the head coach. After the report was released, Russini gave a statement saying she stood by her reporting . It would be hard to imagine Russini returning to the public eye without addressing the situation in some way, but news writers and commentators like Florio are already making it clear she will have to earn back trust beyond a simple statement. What's even crazier is that Texas A&M racked up 457 total yards on offense without scoring 10 points for the first time since facing Texas in 1995. Again, Marcel Reed played better than expected, but in a game where the quarterback must elevate his team, the second-year starter let them down once again. item.description: FOXBOROUGH - On a scale of 1-to-10, Rob Gronkowski predicted his Hall of Fame ceremony would be an 8.7 on the fun meter. It was understandable that Gronk would make a play on his No. 87 jersey number. But this ceremony, from start to finish, was more like a 10. It was a party, or in Gronk terms: “Yo soy fiesta!” To no surprise, it got a little crazy and off the rails at times. And with thousands braving the rainy weather, and lining Patriot Place from above and below, Gronkowski enjoyed every minute. “It meant everything, it really did to have the thousands and thousands of fans here that came out to celebrate this Hall of Fame induction,” Gronkowski told the media following the event. “The fans, I talked about it, they’re the ones who created the Gronk persona because they loved it so much. They’re the ones who created the Gronk spike ... they loved it so much, I had to keep doing it.” Before the ceremony, Gronkowski was out on the plaza, engaging with fans. At one point, he spiked a Green Bay helmet ahead of the Patriots hosting the Packers on Sunday. Along with Gronkowski friends and family members, there were more than 60 Patriots alumni in the house including Tom Brady. With team owner Robert Kraft unable to attend due to recent back surgery, Jonathan Kraft did the honors and introduced Gronkowski. “His play on the field was extraordinary. It was otherworldly, but it was his infectious energy and it was his consistent positive presence that truly set him apart from anybody else who played here,” Kraft said. “The optimism and enthusiasm that he brought into this building every day helped us win because it inspired the other people in the building to be as good as they can be. “And I’m not just talking about the other players and the coaches. Smith drew outrage from Buffalo Bills fans after video showed him grabbing quarterback Josh Allen’s facemask and twisting his head on a goal-line touchdown during Buffalo’s 36-10 win last Sunday. The play wasn’t flagged, which led some to call for the league to suspend him. On Saturday, the NFL did hand down a punishment. The league didn’t suspend Smith, but it hit him where it hurts: his wallet. And it turns out the facemask on Allen (video here) wasn’t the only play from that game that cost him. Roquan Smith Hit With 2 Fines From Bills Game Getty Baltimore Ravens LB Roquan Smith is under fire for what he did to Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen on Sunday The NFL disciplined Smith with $17,911 fine for unnecessary roughness (facemask) on Allen. He was also fined another $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player when he hit Bills wide receiver DJ Moore across the middle in the first quarter. That play wasn’t flagged either. All told, Smith will pay $35,822 for his actions against Buffalo. “Roquan Smith of the Ravens was fined $17,911 for his pulling of the helmet/facemask of Bills QB Josh Allen last Sunday,” Bills reporter Sal Capaccio reported . “The amount is because it was Smith’s second offense this season. He had previously been fined $11,941 for this same infraction in Week 2.” The NFL fined Ravens LB Roquan Smith $17,911 for a facemask — twisting Josh Allen’s head on this TD last week — and another $17,911 for a hit on a defenseless player on a different play. pic.twitter.com/nAJEue4k8S — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 7, 2026 The Allen play came on the Bills’ opening drive. After the Ravens stopped him on third down, Allen went back to the QB sneak on fourth down and pushed across the goal line. As he did, Smith grabbed his facemask and twisted his head with a lot of force. Allen popped up and shoved Ravens cornerback Chidobe Awuzie , but he didn’t appear to be hurt. He stayed in the game and finished with two touchdown passes and a rushing score. Bills head coach Joe Brady said he didn’t even know about the play until after the game. Once he saw it though, Brady said whether intentional or not, it’s “not something you want to see in football.” He added that he was surprised there was no penalty, while acknowledging, “That’s obviously not my place.” Roquan Smith Has Done This Before Getty Baltimore Ravens LB Roquan Smith was fined for two plays against the Buffalo Bills What made Smith’s play on Allen look even worse is that it wasn’t the first time he’s done it
